<p class="name">Joris Klingen</p>
<p class="role">Economist at CPB Netherlands Bureau for Economic Policy Analysis</p>

::: {.chips}
<span>Transport</span><span>Urban</span><span>Environmental</span><span>Energy</span><span>Road safety</span><span>Cycling</span>
:::
:::

<img src="images/joris.png" class="portrait" alt="Portrait of Joris Klingen">
:::

At CPB, I study household energy use, such as responses to energy prices and the adoption of solar panels.
I hold a PhD from [Spatial Economics](https://spatialeconomics.nl/) at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, supervised by Jos van Ommeren and Erik Verhoef.
I studied at the [Tinbergen Institute](https://www.tinbergen.nl), the VU and the Universiteit van Amsterdam, and visited Dan Graham at Imperial College London's [Transport Strategy Centre](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/transport-engineering/transport-strategy-centre/) in 2019.

My research interests are in transport, urban and environmental economics, in particular cycling, road safety and air pollution.
I mostly use natural experiments and large public datasets, such as trip data from bike-sharing schemes in Paris, London and New York.
See [Research](research.qmd) for papers and work in progress.

I'm also a musician: I play keys in [Flamingo Hitmix](https://flamingohitmix.com), drums in [Bovenburen](https://bovenburen.com), and I develop music software (see [Music](music.qmd)).
